chapter_title: Concerning the Three Things that are great with Mankind, as they are running all the time, in that they [ ... ]
chapter_note: No recoverable oldest teaching core is present. The chapter is dominated by hagiographic self-presentation and a Christian-connection comparison (name of Christ used in speech/naming/oaths → likewise Mani’s name), with formulaic opening and apostolic rhetoric. The strong editorial-fatigue signal aligns with institutional/hagiographic expansion rather than cosmological-systematic exposition.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic opening (“Once again he speaks”) plus address to “Christian people” situates this as later editorial/hagiographic framing with Christian connection, not impersonal cosmological exposition.
Explicitly centers the ‘name of Christ’ as invoked over actions; this material enters via Christian tradition/NT milieu (christian_connection), not the pre-compilation cosmological teaching core.
Continues the Christian practice theme (naming people/children by Christ’s name). Christian overlay content rather than systematic cosmological mechanics.
Oath-taking ‘by his fortune and his surety’ under Christ’s authority continues the Christian-practice comparison; not a cosmological mapping or process description.

First-person hagiographic self-identification (“I, Manichaios…”) and apostolic authorization (“Father… sent me”) are compilation-frame rhetoric. Even where ‘Father’ language appears, it functions to legitimate Mani’s mission, not to expound a cosmological system.
Self-exalting rhetoric, apostle-comparison, ‘new aeon’ inheritance promise; institutional/hagiographic voice rather than the impersonal, numbered cosmological-correspondential teaching layer.
